package_info.package_versions: <=2.7.3 (critical RCE with FastJSON gadget); <=2.7.6 (RCE with other gadgets, implementation dependent); <=2.7.9 (unsafe deserialization possible with additional packages)
package_info.why_malicious: The package allows unauthenticated remote code execution via unsafe deserialization of attacker-controlled data in the default Dubbo protocol, due to the ability to select insecure deserializers (Kryo/FST) and the lack of strict class whitelisting. This enables attackers to send crafted binary streams that result in arbitrary code execution on the server.

execution_context.trigger: network request (runtime, upon receiving a Dubbo protocol request)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
byte[] maliciousStream = buildDubboStreamWithPreambleAndFlags(
  preamble = 0xdabb,
  flags = selectKryoOrFST,
  length = ...,
  service = 'dummy',
  method = 'dummy',
  argType = 'java/lang/Object',
  argument = <Kryo/FST-serialized FastJSON gadget chain>
); // Sent over TCP to exposed Dubbo port
malicious_snippets.code_language: java (binary protocol, exploit built in any language)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the server receives a specially crafted Dubbo protocol binary stream with manipulated flags to select an insecure deserializer (Kryo/FST), which then deserializes an attacker-supplied gadget chain, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data using insecure deserializers (Kryo/FST) is a well-known vector for remote code execution. The ability to select the deserializer via a protocol flag is highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict deserialization to safe, whitelisted classes and use a secure deserializer (e.g., Hessian2 with blacklisting). Here, the protocol allows arbitrary deserializer selection and deserializes attacker-controlled objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be internal RPC between trusted services, never exposed to untrusted input or allowing deserializer selection by the client.
key_indicators: Protocol flag allows client to select deserializer
Deserialization of untrusted data without strict class whitelisting
Presence of known gadget chains (e.g., FastJSON) in the argument payload
No authentication or validation on incoming requests

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon deserialization of method argument in Dubbo protocol)

malicious_snippets.code_language: java (serialized object, can be generated in any language)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the deserializer processes the attacker-supplied gadget chain, which triggers arbitrary code execution (e.g., launching calc.exe or running arbitrary commands) on the Dubbo server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserialization of attacker-controlled objects that trigger code execution is a classic RCE pattern. The use of known gadget chains (e.g., FastJSON, JdbcRowSetImpl) is a strong indicator of exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal argument deserialization should only accept safe, expected types. Here, arbitrary objects are deserialized, enabling code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; deserializing untrusted objects from the network is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Deserialization of objects with @type fields or known gadget classes
No input validation or class whitelisting

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a Dubbo protocol binary stream with manipulated flags to select an insecure deserializer (Kryo/FST) and embeds a malicious gadget chain as the method argument.
attack_chain.leads_to: Dubbo server receives and parses the malicious stream.

attack_chain.action: Dubbo server processes the incoming request, reads the protocol preamble, flags, and headers, and invokes the selected deserializer on the method argument.
The deserializer (Kryo/FST) executes the attacker-supplied gadget chain, resulting in arbitrary code execution (e.g., launching calc.exe or running arbitrary commands) on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote code execution on the Dubbo server.

behavioral_signatures: Dubbo protocol requests with non-default deserializer flags (Kryo/FST)
Deserialization of objects with suspicious @type fields or known gadget classes
Unexpected process execution (e.g., calc.exe, /bin/sh) by the Dubbo service
Inbound TCP connections to Dubbo port from untrusted sources
file_indicators: Presence of dubbo-serialization-kryo or dubbo-serialization-fst packages in classpath
Dubbo protocol handler code that allows deserializer selection via protocol flag
network_indicators: Unusual or malformed Dubbo protocol traffic (e.g., non-Hessian2 deserializer flag)
Inbound connections to Dubbo service port (default 20880) from external/untrusted IPs
Outbound connections initiated by the Dubbo service (e.g., RMI, HTTP to attacker-controlled domains)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Dubbo service ports for protocol requests with non-default deserializer flags (Kryo/FST). Inspect deserialized objects for suspicious types or known gadget chains. Alert on unexpected process execution by the Dubbo service. Audit classpath for insecure serialization packages. Restrict network access to Dubbo ports and enforce strict class whitelisting in deserialization logic.
